title: 1924 KLM Fokker F.III disappearance
summary: A Fokker F.III carrying pilot Adriaan Pijl and two passengers departed Lympne, Kent at 13:34 en route to Rotterdam in foggy conditions. The aircraft had previously diverted to Lympne from Croydon due to fog. The aircraft was not equipped with radio and failed to arrive at destination. The investigative committee concluded that the pilot must have hit the water flying at full speed under the fog, as evidenced by a witness who saw the plane at Sandgate in good visibility but noted that fog over the sea obscured the horizon.
probable_cause: The pilot struck the water at full speed under dense fog conditions over the English Channel, with fog obscuring the horizon preventing visual reference for safe navigation.

factors.evidence: foggy conditions and fog over the sea obscured the horizon
the pilot must have hit the water flying at full speed under the fog
the plane was not found, and is presumed to have crashed into the Channel

events.text: Aircraft departed Croydon Airport with pilot Adriaan Pijl and two passengers; foggy conditions forced stopover at Lympne Airport
Aircraft departed Lympne headed for Waalhaven in Rotterdam; not equipped with radio
Witness at Sandgate saw aircraft in good visibility but fog over the sea obscured the horizon from view
Pilot hit the water flying at full speed under the fog; aircraft and all three occupants disappeared and are presumed lost in English Channel

notes: aircraft never found, conclusion based on investigative committee statement and witness account

title: 1924 Imperial Airways de Havilland DH.34 crash
summary: Imperial Airways de Havilland DH.34 G-EBBX crashed at Purley while taking off for Paris from Croydon Airport on Christmas Eve. The aircraft had a long takeoff run, gained altitude slowly, and stalled from 300 ft. A long takeoff run of 700 yards, uphill slope, and sodden grass runway restricted acceleration and climb performance.
probable_cause: The aircraft took off from a sodden grass runway on an uphill slope with restricted acceleration. Environmental conditions combined with aircraft weight near maximum allowable limit resulted in insufficient climb performance and aerodynamic stall. Investigation determined no mechanical defect in the engine.

factors.evidence: rain in the days before the accident had left the grass runways sodden, which would have caused heavy aircraft to sink in and retarded acceleration on take-off
the aircraft took off with a payload of 1560 lb, just under the maximum allowable 1572 lb from a sodden uphill runway
the aircraft only gained height slowly and a witness who saw the take-off from Croydon stated that the take-off run was long, at 700 yd
witnesses stated that the aircraft had stalled from an altitude of 300 ft

events.text: Aircraft takes off from Croydon on scheduled flight to Paris with payload of 1560 lb just under maximum 1572 lb
Takeoff run is long at 700 yards and aircraft only gains height slowly on sodden grass runway
Aircraft stalled from an altitude of 300 ft and nosedives toward ground near Castle Hill, Purley
Aircraft crashes at Purley, overturns, and catches fire; all eight people on board killed

notes: text is incomplete; probable cause not fully stated but environmental factors clear; investigation determined no mechanical defect in engine
